Definition: Shual, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Shual is both a man and a place. One Shual was a son of Zophah in Asher's genealogy, and the land of Shual was the road one company of Philistine raiders took from their camp. The same word names a son and a stretch of country.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe places and people share names because both belong to God. Shual the man and Shual the land are one word, and I hold that the Lord knows His people by name and His land by name too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
